title: Add LTS/release-branch benchmark workflows and gate summary artifact
author: Marcus Reed
description: This PR adds first-class benchmarking workflows intended for Runtime LTS + release branches and produces a gateable summary artifact that Release Eng can use during patch week. Motivation: today we run perf-canary ad-hoc and interpret results manually. For LTS we need something repeatable: (1) a reusable workflow that can be invoked from the runtime release branch CI, (2) a deterministic set of benchmark suites + hardware matrix, and (3) a single "pass/fail + deltas" artifact that is easy to review and attach to go/no-go. What ships here: new GitHub Actions workflows in perf-canary that support workflow_call + workflow_dispatch, a small gate-evaluator that compares results against a pinned baseline, and a renderer that emits both machine-readable JSON and human-readable Markdown. The gate logic is intentionally conservative and does not set final thresholds in this PR (that is handled in a follow-up tuning PR); here we focus on artifact shape + integration points. Release managers will be able to grab the artifact from the run, link it in Slack/Confluence, and attach it to the release PR checklist. Example artifact names: gate-summary.json (for automation) and gate-summary.md (for humans).
commits: ci: add reusable workflow for release-branch benchmarks
bench: add gate evaluator + baseline comparison helpers
report: render gate summary markdown + json
docs: document invocation from runtime release branches
files_changed: .github/workflows/bench-release-branch.yml (new: reusable workflow_call entrypoint, plus workflow_dispatch inputs: runtime_ref, baseline_ref, suite, gpu_matrix)
.github/workflows/bench-release-branch-nightly.yml (new: scheduled sanity run to validate runners + artifact formatting)
suites/release_branch.yaml (new: canonical suites for LTS gating: mixed-length chat, long-context chat, throughput sweep)
baselines/README.md (updated: baseline pinning and how to cut a new baseline for an LTS line)
scripts/evaluate_gate.py (new: compares current results vs baseline and emits pass/fail + deltas)
lib/result_loader.py (updated: accept "release_branch" result schema + stricter validation)
docs/release-branch-gates.md (new: how Release Eng uses artifacts; how to rerun; how to interpret deltas)
conversation: Jonas Weber (review): The artifact format looks good. Two asks: (1) ensure the gate evaluator fails the job when required suites are missing (we’ve had partial uploads), and (2) please include baseline commit SHA in the summary so it’s auditable for LTS.

Marcus Reed (author): Good call. Added schema validation + explicit "required_suites" list and wired missing suite to hard fail. Also included baseline_ref_resolved (full SHA) in both gate-summary.json and gate-summary.md.

Claire Dubois (review): Can we make the GPU matrix explicit and not rely on defaults? Release week we’ll want A100-80GB + H100-80GB as separate lines, and we should record runner type + driver/cuda versions in the summary.

Marcus Reed (author): Updated workflow inputs so callers must specify gpu_matrix, and added runner metadata capture (nvidia-smi, driver, cuda, container image digest) into the summary. The metadata lives under a "provenance" section in markdown and as flat keys in JSON.

Allison Grant (review): From an SRE perspective, we need a clear rerun story when runners are contended. Can we mark the summary with a "noisy run" flag when we detect high variance between repeated subruns?

Marcus Reed (author): Implemented a basic variance check for the throughput sweep subruns and a noisy_run=true marker when coefficient of variation exceeds a small threshold. It doesn’t fail the gate by itself; it’s informational until thresholds are finalized in ENG-4825 follow-ups.

Connor O'Brien (review): Please align naming with the release checklist: artifact should be called lts-gate-summary.* not gate-summary.* to avoid confusion when multiple artifacts are attached. Also ensure workflow_call outputs include an artifact URL we can paste into the release PR.

Marcus Reed (author): Renamed artifacts to lts-gate-summary.json/md and added a step that prints the Actions run URL + artifact name in the job summary. workflow_call now exposes outputs: gate_status, summary_artifact_name, run_url.
Jonas Weber (approve): Looks ready. Let’s keep thresholds out of this PR; follow-up PR can tighten p95 regressions once we’ve validated stability on real runners.
Connor O'Brien (approve): Approved. This unblocks wiring perf-canary into the runtime LTS patch runbook.
release_notes: Internal: perf-canary now supports release-branch/LTS gating workflows with a standardized summary artifact (JSON + Markdown).
final_merge_summary: Merged via squash. Release managers can now run perf-canary against a runtime release branch ref and receive a single lts-gate-summary artifact with baseline SHA, deltas, provenance, and a gate pass/fail status suitable for LTS patch go/no-go.
